title: readpdb: triclinic cell from stdin, no dihedrals
purpose: Exercises the cell and input-validation branches of `readpdb` [@pdbformat,@epsrmanual]: a valid triclinic `CRYST1` record followed by one whose angle field cannot be read, so the cell is asked on standard input; an invalid van der Waals factor replaced by the default; no dihedral groups; one molecule per residue without `CONECT` records.
fortran: `readpdb.f`: `run_readpdb`, `readpdb` (CRYST1/ATOM/CONECT records, molecules from residues, bonds from van der Waals radii, angle constraints, DIH groups), `upcase`
system: Four molecules (23 atoms) in a triclinic cell a, b, c = 21, 23.5, 26.25 Å, alpha, beta, gamma = 80°, 96°, 110° (EPSR cell angles 110°, 10.380°, 125.462° in the header): a water, a dimethyl sulphoxide, a TIP4P-like water whose dummy site becomes a `Q` atom, and a methanol. Bonds are found where the distance is below 0.7 × the sum of the van der Waals radii, and bond-angle constraints are generated.
inputs: `cluster.pdb` from a helper script (a one-off script that was not kept; the generated file is the input); the second `CRYST1` record has angle `8x.00`. `readpdb cluster < readpdb.stdin` (no extension): cell `21.0 23.5 26.25 80.0 96.0 110.0`, factor `0` (invalid -> 0.7), dihedrals `no`. `vanderWaalsRadii.txt` copied from EPSR-test.
verification: Output compared: `cluster.ato`. Fortran reference: the original `readxyz`/`readpdb` binaries crash (SIGSEGV) at the first call of `ctype`, which has optional arguments but is called with 11 of its 13 arguments without an explicit interface (gfortran passes the hidden character lengths where `radmaxsph`/`pseudofacsph` are expected). The reference was therefore produced with an explicit `INTERFACE` block for `ctype` added to the program (no other change; absent arguments mean `radmaxsphere = 0.5*sigcor`, `pseudofacmol = 1`), built by `rust/tools/build_patched_readxyz_readpdb.sh`; the comparison is against this patched build, not the original binary.
